Hon'ble
Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 18/08/2023
1.

The accused/appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14 (A) (2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short "the SC/ST Act ") for grant of anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.18/2021 registered at Police Station Dharamjaigarh,
District Raigarh for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(N), 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act.

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Prosecution case in brief is that on 27.05.2023 the prosecutrix lodged the written report alleging in it that the applicant came her rented house and made physical relationship with her on the pretext of marriage, subsequently, the applicant refused to marry with her and on the basis of written report FIR lodged against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant would submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

He would further submit that the victim is aged about 33 years old major lady and well aware of the consequences of physical relationship and the evidence of the prosecutrix is not supported by medical report.
He was the consenting party, therefore, the appellant may be granted anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the state opposes the anticipatory bail application of the appellant and would submit that the challan has been filed before the trial Court with the stipulated Aashish Kumar Dansena vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170438041/
1 time, therefore, the applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
5.

entities.text: Aashish Kumar Dansena vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the last date of hearing i.e. on 11.08.2023, the prosecutrix appeared before this Court and stated that she has no objection, if the bail is granted to the appellant.
6. I have heard counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

7. Considering the entire facts situation of the case and the fact that the prosecutrix is a major lady and well aware of the consequence of physical relationship, further considering the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 CrPC, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the appellant.
8. Accordingly, the criminal appeal is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest of appellant in connection with Crime No. 133/2023 registered at PS Dharamjaigarh, Distt. Raigarh (CG), he will be released on bail by the arresting officer on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 25,000/-
with one local surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting offence with following further conditions :
(i) that he shall make himself available for interrogation before the investigating officer as and when required;
(ii) that he shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer.

(iii) that he shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial; and (iv) that he shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial;
